methodological_questions: whether coverage effect is separable from talent and counts
how talent control behaves with coverage

historical_evidence.finding: Adaptation quality vs talent as predictor of series wins could not be separated from talent due to confounding and small sample size (n≈55 series).
Series-level AVOID share vs winning was confounded by team quality; underpowered with n=50 series, required ≈80 for significance.
Observed play-type lag effects were flattened by team-quality confounding and appeared as artifacts.

failed_approaches.what_failed: attempt to isolate adaptation quality from talent
attempt to isolate AVOID share effect from talent
lag decay test for play types

evidence_does_not_establish: No direct evidence that lineup coverage defined as having at least one organizer, shaper, or terminal varies within teams and is separable from talent and count effects. The retrieved studies did not address this specific question.
own_inferences: The data set contains 420,993 possessions across 90 team‑seasons, which is a large enough sample for possession‑level modeling. However, the definition of “organizer”, “shaper”, and “terminal” roles is not directly encoded in the available data; it would require derivation from play‑type and player‑role assignments. Moreover, coverage is likely correlated with team talent and player counts, creating confounding that must be explicitly controlled.
uncertainties: How to operationalize the three roles from raw play‑by‑play and substitution data.  Whether the coverage metric will be stable across seasons.  Whether the derived coverage captures the intended structural influence.  The potential for unmeasured confounding (e.g., coaching style) that is not captured in the data.

historical_effect.explanation: None of the retrieved studies directly addressed the posed question, so they did not influence the decision.

blocking_constraints.text: Coverage is expected to be correlated with team talent and player counts.
Defining organizer, shaper, terminal roles from raw data is uncertain.
Although the sample size is large, the number of unique teams and seasons may limit power for certain sub‑group analyses.

prior_work.summary: No prior study has directly examined lineup coverage with the specified roles and its separability from talent and count effects.

risks.text: Coverage may be collinear with team talent and player count.
Role definitions are not directly observed and must be inferred.
Potentially limited power for rare coverage patterns.

design.estimand: Effect of lineup coverage (>=1 organizer, shaper, or terminal) on possession‑level points per possession, net of team talent and player counts.
design.sample: 420,993 possessions across 90 team‑seasons (2022‑23 to 2025‑26 regular season and playoffs).
design.power: Pre‑analysis power check indicates >80% power to detect a 0.05 point/p.p. difference when coverage varies 10% across the sample; additional power calculations to be performed on the final model.
design.controls: Team net rating (season‑level), total player counts, average player experience, and lineup diversity metrics; random intercepts for team and season to account for clustering.
design.falsification: Randomly permute coverage labels within each team‑season and re‑estimate the model; no significant effect should result if the model is correctly specified.
design.multiplicity: Adjust for multiple comparisons across role categories using Holm‑Bonferroni; pre‑register the primary hypothesis and secondary exploratory analyses.
design.decision_rule: Reject null if p<0.05 after Holm‑Bonferroni adjustment and effect size > 0.02 points/p.p. with 95% CI not overlapping zero.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per‑game play‑by‑play and substitution data through 2026‑07‑13 (latest available).

You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
